title: Using mathematical modeling in training planning
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Not applicable (critical discussion of systems modelling of training effects on performance)
findings: Discusses strengths and weaknesses of systems modelling for analysing training effects on performance.

The simplifications inherent to the approach are outlined: choice of input and output variables, model structure, data collection for parameter estimation, and use of identified models to predict responses.

Despite insight into the effects of intensifying or reducing training, the existing models would not be accurate enough to make predictions for a particular athlete in order to monitor his or her training.
limitations: Narrative critique from 2006, before regularised, Bayesian and ML approaches; no new data.
implications: Use the model for explanation and scenario comparison (what-if taper or load-shape), not for individual race-time prediction.
Document model inputs (load metric), outputs (performance test) and structure explicitly in the engine, since these are the stated sources of error.
